description: Focos builds one fire record for Argentina from MODIS and VIIRS. VIIRS reports several detections where MODIS reported one, so a record stitched from the two jumps in 2012. Focos converts VIIRS to MODIS-equivalent counts, checks the result on years the method never saw, and shows it as a monthly fire calendar for any province or drawn area since 2003.
summary: Focos turns NASA FIRMS hotspots from MODIS (Aqua) and VIIRS (S-NPP, then NOAA-20) into one fire record for Argentina, from 2003 to today. Joined as they are, the two sensors make Argentina's fire count jump from 45,740 in 2011 to 167,274 in 2012, a rise no fire caused: VIIRS simply sees much smaller fires. Focos counts every sensor in the same unit, the 1 km fire cell-pass, then converts VIIRS down to MODIS-equivalent counts with a ratio for each 5° region, season and time of day. We chose and froze the method on 2012-2019 and tested it once on 2020-2021, years it never saw: the typical error of a province's monthly count fell from 432% for the naive stitch to 17%. The free web app, in English and Spanish, lets anyone pick a province, draw an area or enter a point, and see when it burns, which years were worst and whether this month is unusual. It is built for provincial fire services, researchers, journalists and students who need to read Argentina's fire history across the change of satellite.
details:
What it does

Focos is a free web app that gives Argentina one consistent fire record from 2003 to the present, built from NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspots from three satellites: Aqua MODIS, VIIRS S-NPP and VIIRS NOAA-20. Pick a province, draw an area or enter a point, and it shows a month-by-month fire calendar, which years were worst, the long-term trend and how unusual the current month is. It works in English and Spanish, and every hotspot behind a number can be downloaded.

The problem

MODIS has watched fires since the early 2000s and is at the end of its life. VIIRS replaces it but sees much smaller fires, so the two records cannot be read as one. Joined as they are, Argentina's fire count jumps from 45,740 in 2011 to 167,274 in 2012. Nothing happened on the ground; the sensor changed.

How it works

  • One counting unit for every sensor: a fire cell-pass is one 0.01° cell (about 1 km), on one local date, by day or by night, seen by one sensor. Several pixels in the same cell-pass count once.
  • Convert VIIRS down to MODIS, never MODIS up: for each 5° block, season and day/night, the ratio k = (M + m·k̄) / (V + m) says how many Aqua cell-passes one VIIRS cell-pass is worth, pulled toward the national ratio where data is thin (m = 200).
  • Every hotspot carries a weight w = k / n, so every count in the app (calendar, map and downloads) is a sum of the same weights.
  • Aqua carries the record to January 2012, S-NPP from February 2012 to October 2026, and NOAA-20 since S-NPP stopped delivering data on 2 November 2026, plus 62 earlier days when S-NPP was out.

How we know it works

Three candidate methods were scored by leave-one-year-out on 2012–2019, a rule set in advance picked the simplest one within 10% of the best, and the model was frozen before any test result was computed. On the held-out years 2020–2021, compared with Aqua MODIS: national monthly bias −0.1% (median error 8.3%), province-month median error 17.0% (naive stitch: 432%) and national log correlation 0.993. All three targets we set in advance were met. NOAA-20 was re-fitted with the same frozen recipe and passed the same test (province-month error 17.5%).

Impact

Read raw, Argentina's record says fire rose about 242% per decade and 22 of 24 provinces are burning more. Harmonized, fire fell about 25% per decade, close to Aqua alone (22%), and only one province is rising. Provincial fire services, researchers, journalists and students can now compare any month with the years before 2012, and with S-NPP retired in November 2026, the bridge to NOAA-20 is already in place.

What makes it different

Focos converts down instead of inventing fires MODIS never saw, tests itself on years it never saw, and shows its limits inside the app: provinces that run high or low in the test (such as Neuquén, where fixed heat sources inflate VIIRS) are flagged, very large fire months are known to be understated, and the "How it works" page reads every number from the validation file. A Raw switch shows the jump the change of sensor puts into the record.

Tools

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, DuckDB, Shapely) for the data pipeline, with 160 tests; TypeScript, Vite, D3 and Leaflet (with Leaflet-Geoman and Turf for drawn areas) for the web app, with unit and page tests in Vitest; hosted free on GitHub Pages. The demo video is rendered from HTML and canvas with headless Chrome and FFmpeg.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

We used Claude (Anthropic) to help in writing the code and building the demo video, and Google Gemini to generate the video’s narration voice. Our team members are under 18, and Space Apps rules don’t allow minors’ faces or voices in project materials, so the video uses an AI voice instead of ours.
